pages.title: International Affairs Team and living guide scope
pages.text:
## International Affairs Team
This DGIST Living Guide is prepared to help new DGIST international members adjust to life in DGIST and Daegu. If you are a student, please refer to 'Campus Life Guide Book' first which is prepared by Student Affairs Team. If you have any comments or suggestions on the contents of this booklet, please contact International Affairs Team.
Published by International Affairs Team, DGIST. Updated in August 2025.
International Affairs Team: irt@dgist.ac.kr.

pages.title: Power plugs and prepaid SIM cards before arrival
pages.text:
## Power plugs
In Korea, the power plugs and sockets are types C and F. The standard voltage is 220V. The outlet with two round holes is also used in countries like France, Germany, Austria, etc.
## Prepaid SIM cards before arrival
Prepaid Sim Cards can be available for use with passports even before obtaining a Residence Card. Purchase and activation are possible at Incheon International Airport and Daegu International Airport. Additionally, activation through visiting an agent after online reservation is also possible. Please make sure to prepare the SimCard/e-Sim before coming to Korea or at the airport since it is quite difficult to get the prepaid SimCard/e-Sim without a Residence Card nearby DGIST.

pages.title: Korean Language Center and Korean language classes
pages.text:
## Korean Language Center
DGIST is expanding our global presence by creating a Bilingual Campus that brings together diverse perspectives. Our Korean Language Center was founded with the idea of encouraging meaningful connections between international students and Korean Students. DGIST believes that through language and culture, we can build a community where everyone grows together.
Homepage: https://www.dgist.ac.kr/klc/
## Korean Language Class overview
DGIST provides Korean language class not only for international students but other international members and their family. Two different levels of classes, one for beginner and the other for post-ginner, are offered per each semester. International students can take the courses after registration and, other members (faculties, researchers, staffs and long-term visitors) and their family can audit the courses.

pages.title: TOPIK preparation, language exchange and Living in Korea lectures
pages.text:
## Summer/Winter Intensive TOPIK Class overview
At DGIST, we are pleased to offer the Intensive TOPIK Class during the vacation period, designed to support international members preparing for the Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK). The course is divided into TOPIK I (beginner) and TOPIK II (intermediate/advanced) levels, focusing on problem-solving and exam preparation. This class provides targeted practice and strategies to help you excel in the TOPIK and improve your Korean language skills effectively.
## Language Exchange Program overview
We are excited to introduce a Language Exchange Program for students at DGIST, who are interested in learning and improving their Korean and English-speaking skills. To create a casual and creative learning experience, we intend to include various games, quizzes, etc., in both Korean and English to facilitate interaction among participants.
## Living in Korea Lecture Series overview
This session is designed to provide useful insights, cultural context, and practical tips to help international members better understand and adjust to life in Korea. This course covers topics related to Korean laws, culture, politics, economy, and society.

pages.title: Buddy Program and orientation for international members
pages.text:
## Buddy Program
Here at DGIST, we welcome our international students through the Buddy program, where we match our students with other existing students. In this program, international students will be provided with a general introduction to life on campus and receive various support for settling in.
## Orientation for International Members
To help international members understand and adjust to life in DGIST and Korea, International Affairs Team (IAT) offers customized orientation to new international members.
Program: Overview on DGIST; facilities and services on Campus and in Daegu area; general guide to campus life; campus tour and campus map.

pages.title: DISA DGIST International Student Association
pages.text:
## DISA International Student Association
DISA, the DGIST International Student Association, established in 2024, is the first official organization representing the international community at DGIST. It supports international students, faculty, researchers, staff, and their families, fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment.
## DISA participation and contact
For those interested in volunteering or participating in DISA activities, you are welcome to visit the Global Lounge (E7-261) or contact us via email.
Email: disa@dgist.ac.kr.
Instagram: @dgist_disa.
Facebook: DGIST International Student Association.
Location: Global Lounge (E7-261).

pages.title: Student dormitory laundry app for international students
pages.text:
## Using a Laundry App at Student Dormitory
For laundry at student dormitory, you should download the app called 'MetaClub', which allows you to pay for the laundry and check the available time and machine. International students or visiting students without a Residence Card can charge the money only with cash at a convenience store. Please see a guide for student without RC.
Dormitory: dormitory@dgist.ac.kr.

pages.title: On-campus apartment inquiries and off-campus housing resources
pages.text:
## On-Campus Apartment inquiry
General Affairs Team. Contact: 053-785-1247, general@dgist.ac.kr.
## Off-Campus Housing resources
There is a residential area in Technopolis, the area around DGIST. There are various types of housing such as apartments, villas, multi-family housings, etc.
If you would like to seek your house outside of campus, you should use a real estate agent or smartphone applications for housing seeking such as Jigbang (직방) and Dabang (다방).
